title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
why_read: A clever architectural idea for improving reinforcement learning in LLMs by separating exploration from the final optimized model.
analysis: The paper tackles a known problem in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, where encouraging a model to explore novel reasoning paths often degrades its overall quality. Their fix trains separate explorer models with a novelty bonus, filters their outputs for correctness, then distills the good ones into a clean student model trained without that novelty pressure. This decoupling lets them scale up exploration aggressively without the usual quality collapse, and they show better results than a strong baseline across seven math benchmarks. This is a practically useful training recipe for anyone building reasoning-focused LLMs via RL.
